Conduct a public hearing and adopt the proposed amendments to the County Drug Paraphernalia Ordinance revising County Code Section 86-106, clarifying definitions to align with recent statutory changes to exclude products for fentanyl analogue and xylazine testing to promote the health, safety, and welfare of residents.
· In 2005, Pinellas County adopted resolution 05-195 to establish a Drug Paraphernalia Abatement Task Force (Task Force) to review community impacts. As a result of Task Force recommendations, the County adopted Ordinance 06-73, to help mitigate possible community impact and limit access by youth.
· Since adopting the ordinance, Pinellas has experienced the impacts of the prescription drug epidemic and the resulting opioid crisis from the illicit drug market, with 266 overdose-related deaths in 2025.
· In recent years, fentanyl, fentanyl analogues, and xylazine have emerged as a major drugs of concern driving overdoses nationwide. Often individuals are unaware of the presence of these substances resulting in severe risk of poisoning, hospitalization, and death.
· In response to this growing threat, the State of Florida passed House Bill 477 revising drug paraphernalia definitions to add exclusions of products for xylazine testing effective July 1, 2026 in order to help reduce possible overdoses and save lives. Fentanyl and fentanyl analogue testing products were excluded by the State of Florida and Pinellas County in 2023.
· Based on the statutory change, Pinellas County is seeking to quickly incorporate the same exclusion locally to help protect the health and safety of our residents.
· Human Services anticipates a full review of this ordinance in the coming year to receive updated stakeholder input, assess updates and ongoing needs, and define recommended changes.
· This ordinance change has no fiscal impact to Pinellas County. Additionally, this change creates no new business impacts.

Recommend adoption of a resolution to not exempt property under the Live Local Act Property Tax Exemption (The Act).

· With the commencement of the 2027 tax roll, taxing authorities may “opt-out” of providing The Act to certain rental units in multifamily projects that would otherwise qualify for the 80.0% to 120.0% Tax Exemption if the previous three (3) years of the Shimberg Center for Housing Studies Annual Report (Shimberg Annual Report) identifies a surplus of affordable and available units.
· On November 18, 2025, the Board of County Commissioners (Board) approved a Resolution to “opt-out” for 2026, but a new resolution is required to continue it through 2027.
· The County finds that the previous three (3) years of the Shimberg Annual Report identifies a surplus of affordable and available units within the Tampa St. Petersburg- Clearwater MSA, in which Pinellas County is located, for those households that meet the income criteria for the 80.0% to 120.0% Tax Exemption.
· Pursuant to Section 196.1978(3)(o), Florida Statutes, the County remains eligible for the “opt-out” election and, pending approval of this Resolution, elects not to exempt properties eligible for the exemption and requests that PAO not grant any such exemptions.
· This Resolution applies to all ad valorem property tax levies imposed by the County. If approved, it will take effect on January 1, 2027, and will expire or be renewed pursuant to the provisions Section 196.1978(3)(o), Florida Statutes.
